original_card.question: Can a template or call contract leave two or more unpaid coordinates per live family?
methods: State a replacement for the coverage identity (mass = 72W + 64N) and the contract change that realizes it, with its implementation cost.
Find an obstruction: show which data-endpoint obligation forces exactly one unpaid coordinate in the current template.
original_card.acceptance_gate: An explicit replacement identity, verified on a small complete instance with dirty inputs, priced with ceiling.ceiling(unpaid=...).

first_step.inspect: Read the selected word's per-call local profile, its packing ceiling and the lever table; run levers.py for the ideal budget of the lever you target.
first_step.scope: Positive control and planning budget only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: Explain where the single unpaid coordinate per family comes from in the hosted template; propose one change and price it. Ideal budget: two unpaid coordinates per family is 3.77x (levers.py).
original_card.bottleneck_link: The deficit is one coordinate per family minus the centre charge; doubling unpaid coordinates per family scales it directly.
allowed_variations: One template change or one endpoint-contract change.
If the coverage law, template or guard changes, derive an applicable fully charged replacement bound instead of applying the incumbent ceiling outside its scope.
scope_change_triggers: Counting a coordinate as unpaid while leaving it unadvanced in the data endpoint.

actual_scope: On the PR2322 T74 words, can the end-of-call restoration climbs of FULL-cleanup helpers (PR2429) be removed by cold restoration under the existing restore-plus-zero-buffer contract, and what is a rigorous frame-only upper bound on that lever?
scope_change_reason: Drawn on the recursive-interfaces track (seed 58: eliminate boundary or restoration work). The concrete restoration item on the live T74 line is PR2429's end-climb lever; the card closest to a changed per-call contract is coverage-law-change, but the object here is restoration work, not unpaid coordinates.
bottleneck_link: Determines whether the largest remaining paid item of pure restoration work on the top T74 words can be removed with existing machinery; it cannot by single-gate moves, and frames cap it at +8.86%.
stop_rule: Stop after the exact single-gate screen, construction plus exact replay of every candidate, and the time-resolved frame bound with its LP price; no multi-gate restoration search.
evidence: restoration_screen.py: 8/355 helpers have a single commuting restoring gate; their converted words (restore + reader clearing at the joined frame + buffer-free cleanup) pass the exact replay forward and dual but the joined frame is FULL for all 8 (saving 0). Loose time-resolved frame estimate caps the lever at 438/525 dims, +8.86% LP ceiling; a reviewer's unreviewed exact span check suggests about 54/525.

open_questions.question: Are there helpers whose input readers all sit at low frames, so that a multi-gate restoration with reader clearing joins below FULL?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Reader-frame joins are what defeat the single-gate moves; only helpers with low-frame readers can still save anything.
open_questions.first_step: Make the span-based bound rigorous (warps after last use included) and rank helpers by reader-frame join.
open_questions.blocked_by: Time-resolved span algebra with operator words.

open_questions.question: Can restoration be placed earlier in B, before the readers' frames grow?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Readers' frames at end of forward are the binding join; earlier placement could lower it.
open_questions.first_step: Compute the reader-frame join at each candidate's last use instead of at the end of forward.
open_questions.blocked_by: Later reads of the readers must then see the restored value; ordering legality unchecked.
